components.gap: Supply (i) the source's justification of the truncation level in Example 3.4.13 (p.151): c_n = n^{1/2} log log n is chosen large enough that sum_m P(Y_{n,m} != X_m) <= nP(|X1| > c_n) -> 0, while the truncation is kept close to the lowest possible level because the variance of Y_{n,m} should be as small as possible; and (ii) the source's hypothesis-replacing Remark on p.152: replacing P(|X1| > x) = x^-2 by x^-alpha with 0 < alpha < 2 gives S_n/n^{1/alpha} converging weakly to a limit which is not chi. thm:p15-clt-infinite-variance-example (parts 330-346, annex 1093-1142) states the level and its two estimates but neither the design rationale nor the alpha < 2 variant; the routed thm:p15-nda-examples item 3 only excludes a normal limit and does not assert convergence at scale n^{1/alpha}. an unrouted treatment exists in handbook/parts/p15/limit-theorems-and-concentration-w02c-p15-015.tex (not \input by handbook/parts/p15.tex, so not counted; its completeness is not assessed here) (thm:p15-w02c-p15-015-truncation-window, thm:p15-w02c-p15-015-power-tail-limit).
